longForm.overview:
🚽 is the emoji of tool coded toilet read — a clean toilet-pulse shape, the tool filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'tool toilet' tag for build-marker. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded toilet read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded toilet read, 🚽 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate tool coded toilet — a 'tool 🚽' build-marker marker or a 'toilet-pulse pulse 🚽' build-marker reveal. The tool fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern build-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as tool coded rather than literal toilet-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🚽 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate build-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'tool 🚽' build-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'toilet-pulse pulse 🚽' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'tool coded 🚽' list thread. The tool fill cue is what makes the emoji feel tool coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'tool coded toilet moment.'

What separates 🚽 from the rest of the shape family is the tool register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'tool coded toilet,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🚽 travels especially well on partner build-marker markers, build-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with tool energy.

In group chats 🚽 anchors 'tool coded moment' threads, build-marker reveals, and 'tool 🚽' tags where the toilet cue matches the register. On Instagram it lands on tool coded flat-lays and tool-canvas stories. On TikTok it travels in tool coded reveals and 'tool' reaction content.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🚽 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The tool coded toilet cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🚽 in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the tool energy feels off. A 'tool 🚽' message works for tool marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🚽 when you want to communicate a different color. The tool coded register is too tool-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🚽, the cleanest mirror is another 🚽, ⬛, or a sentence that joins the tool energy. If you want to escalate the engagement, follow with a sentence that adds context: 'tool for sure' or 'toilet-pulse pulse together.' If the toilet cue feels too tool coded, reply with a sharper emoji (◼ or ◻) that signals shape-coded energy without matching the tool volume.

When 🚽 lands as a partner 'tool 🚽' build-marker marker, mirror with another 🚽, a heart emoji, or a sentence that escalates the romance. When it arrives as a 'toilet-pulse pulse 🚽' list thread, mirror with another 🚽, a sentence that joins the team energy, or a heart emoji that matches.
